decisions.what_changed: A: a not-measured spoke no longer pulls the curve down to the inner clamp (where -3 SD is drawn). When every spoke is measured the crisp curve, the +/-1 SD band and the 20 fuzz curves are closed, as before (byte-identical paths for the full profile). Otherwise each run of measured neighbours is an open curve (d3 curveCatmullRom.alpha(0.5), then curveCardinal.tension(0.6), then curveLinear, under the same 0.1-ring overshoot rule, curve.ts). The band and each fuzz band are one closed region per run: one edge forward, the other edge backwards. A lone measured spoke (no measured neighbour) has no curve, band or fuzz; its marker and 90% whisker still show the estimate and its range. The gap marker moved from a ring at the centre to an x on the 0 SD ring (two strokes at 45 degrees to the spoke, arm 4.5 user units, in the stub colour over a halo in the page background). The grey stub at the centre and the dashed spoke stay (section 9.7). The stub and the x are placeholders, not data, so they are drawn in their own group ('g.stubs', each still a 'g.mark.unmeasured') under the ring labels: where an x meets a ring label at phone sizes the label's halo covers part of the x and the label stays readable (the data's marks stay above the labels, UX-045). The tier (c) hatch now fills model.hatchFill: the closed curve when there are no gaps; otherwise each run's curve closed through the centre, and a narrow sector up to the marker for a lone spoke. STUB_CAPTION now says the line breaks there and the x is not an estimate. B: when the default text layout does not fit the chart's width (narrow screens; also very large text) and 5 or more spokes are not measured, those spokes get no label and a line under the chart (inside BlobChart.svelte, after the svg, as HTML text that grows with the text size) names them: 'Not measured: <full names>.' (facets: 'Insufficient data: ...'). With bare stubs the viewBox fits the labels left on each side, so the circle can sit off centre and grows. Measured, m1 (10 of 17 not measured): rings across 71% / 69% / 65% of the chart at 390 / 360 / 320 px (before about 42% at 390), smallest chart text 11.01 px at all three (before about 9.5-10 px at 320). The share card has no not-measured spokes (only measured skills the person left on are drawn; hidden skills are re-spread, not gapped), so A has nothing to change there; the card's blob is built by the same buildBlob.

deviations: B uses 'none' (no label on a not-measured spoke), not short labels: measured first, short names alone free no width, because the labels of the measured spokes set the (centred) viewBox. The room comes from letting the viewBox fit each side's own labels when the stubs are bare, so on phones the circle may sit off centre.

'Narrow screen' is 'the default text layout does not fit at this width' (the case where fitLayout has to adapt), not 'compact labels were chosen': WebKit measures narrower glyphs and kept full labels at 390 px, which would have left the iPhone chart unchanged.

A lone measured spoke between two gaps has no curve, band or fuzz; its marker and 90% whisker are its uncertainty mark. A lone tier (c) spoke's hatch is a narrow sector (half a spoke gap wide) up to its marker.
The grey stub at the centre (section 9.7) is kept; only the dip and the gap marker changed.

The not-measured marks moved from the 'g.marks' group (drawn after the data) to a 'g.stubs' group drawn between the grid and the ring labels; selectors 'g.mark.unmeasured ...' and the count of 17 'g.mark' still hold.

decisions.what_changed: On the share card a credible low (90% range below 0 SD) is drawn muted, like a range that overlaps 0 SD (hollow grey marker or arrow, grey whisker, grey curve run, label in the plain text colour), so the only strong colour on the card marks a range above 0 SD (card.ts cardSpoke; the page keeps the section 9.5 rule). The named peaks (the ones the card lists) are ringed (a circle r = 9 user units round the marker, in the blob colour) and their labels bold; buildBlob takes the peak ids (BlobOptions.peaks, SpokeView.peak), so BlobChart.svelte draws the same marks for the card's model and the card/page twin test still compares element by element. The key now reads 'Filled: range above 0 SD. Hollow: range overlaps or is below 0 SD.' plus ' Ringed: a named peak.' when the card lists peaks (one row of 88 characters, at most 96). To keep it one row, 'SD means standard deviation.' moved to the last row, after the two ring-note lines. The small print keeps its 5 rows, so the chart region (704 x 472 card px) is unchanged. gated.json has no request to this package; its D2 card note still wraps to 91 / 90 / 41 characters on 3 rows.
